paper.title: Evaluating exact VARMA likelihood and its gradient when data are incomplete
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 35(1), 2008, article 6 (Algorithm 878; the archive header 878.head says TOMS vol. 35 no. 1 2008 article 6)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 878.zip (scouted 2026-11-27, sha256 cbf6aec91cef72ae3c71af66c31274d4c76ac5c88f68acd2fef69a1001afd337). Contains Matlab/Src (varma_llc.m and private functions), Matlab/Tests/test/compare (comparison.txt, as311.c, jam197.for, compare_with_as311.m) and Doc/ (manuscript method.pdf, demorunoutput.pdf).

claim.location: Shipped reference file Matlab/Tests/test/compare/comparison.txt (inside 878.zip). Its table 'COMPARING VARMA_LLC WITH ALGORITHM AS-311', column varma_llc: the value of the complete-data VARMA log-likelihood that Matlab/Src/varma_llc.m returns for each of ten test cases (tinyAR ... mediumARMA2). The paper itself does not print these numbers: its numerical results are timings in Tables I and II (machine-dependent, not claimed) and it says the Matlab numerical results are in a companion paper.
claim.metric: varma_llc log-likelihood value for each of the ten named test cases in compare_with_as311.m (the varma_llc column of comparison.txt), with the test problems as defined in test_varma_llc.m.
claim.paper_value: Not in the paper; the shipped comparison.txt is the only value to check.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference prints 9 decimal places, so its rounding unit is 1e-9. The as311 agreement recorded in the same file is 2e-15 relative. A tolerance of 1e-6 absolute (about 2e-8 relative at magnitude 50) allows for floating-point differences between the Matlab/Octave runtimes, but is far below the 9-decimal rounding of the printed values' differences between test cases.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: ten varma_llc evaluations on small problems (n up to a few hundred). Needs MATLAB, or Octave with a mex-compatible build of as311.c and jam197.for only if the rerun also reproduces the comparison column; the varma_llc column alone needs only the Matlab/Src files and the test data in Matlab/Tests/test.
cost.data_size: Archive 328 KB-class zip, test data generated in code (no external data beyond temperature.dat for demorun, not used by this claim).
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a Collected Algorithms (ACM TOMS) program.

why: varma_llc is the complete-data exact VARMA likelihood the paper describes (Cholesky plus Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury in the paper's method); the archive's comparison with the published AS 311 program gives ten independent log-likelihood values that the code has to compute, so the claim tests the code, not a closed form.
